Title: Animation Keyframe and Layer Editing (ver. 12)
Content: Objective The inclusion of keyframes for simulation caches and keyframe editing tools allow users to fix isolated simulation issues, blend simulations together, adjust timing, and create looping cloth simulation caches. Edit Animation Keyframes Location Animation Editor Animation Timeline Operation Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. Select the Animation Layer created for the garment in the Animation Timeline Where vertical lines exist marking Keyframes, select a Keyframe and delete it by pressing the 'Delete' Key. Observe that there is no longer a Keyframe in the previously selected position, and the simulation interpolates vertex positions for the garment linearly across the gap. Where there is now an empty space between Keyframes, move the playtime slider to this position. Select a pattern or garment in the 3D Window. Using the Gizmo, rotate or translate the pattern/garment into a new position. The user can also activate simulation in the 3D Window before creating a new Keyframe. While the playtime slider is still at the position without a keyframe, add a new Keyframe with the 'S' Hotkey. Slide the playtime slider across the area of the timeline where a new frame was keyed, and observe the saved change in the updated frame keyed by the user. To form a smoother transition between the preexisting cache animation and the user-created Keyframe, delete simulation cache Keyframes to the left and right of the user-created Keyframe. Note: Fit the Frame Range - Click the 'Fit Horizontal' button located next to the 'Animation Max Frame' input field at the bottom right of the Animation Editor. This will display every animation layer from its start to end. - Double-click the Animation timeslider to switch to the full layer view. (ver.2024.0) Copy &amp Paste Keyframes Location Animation Editor Animation Timeline Operation Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. 'LMB Click' to select a single Keyframe, or 'Shift + LMB Click and Drag' to select multiple Keyframes. If a range of Keyframes has been selected, the user can 'LMB Click and Drag' the white handles on either side of the selection to make fine adjustments. Once the desired selection has been achieved, 'RMB Click' over the highlighted selection to open a pop-up menu then select 'Copy Keyframe' to store the selected frame(s). Move the playtime slider to a different position on the timeline in the same Animation Layer and 'RMB Click' then select 'Paste Keyframe' to past the Keyframe(s) beginning from the current position. Animation Editor Keyframe Options: Create Keyframe 'S' Delete Keyframe 'Del' Copy Keyframe 'Ctrl+C' Paste Keyframe 'Ctrl+V' Cut &amp Merge Animation Layer Location Animation Editor Animation Timeline Operation Cut Animation Layer Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. Select the resulting Animation Layer by clicking on its title at the left of the Animation Editor interface. Move the playtime slider to a point in the middle of the resulting Animation Layer. Press the 'Cut' button in the Animation Editor Toolbar (scissor icon). Observe that the Animation Layer has split at the current timeline position, and the portion removed has been separated into a new Animation Layer. Merge Animation Layers Select two Animation layers by clicking on their titles at the left of the Animation Editor interface while holding the 'Shift' Key. Press the 'Merge' button in the Animation Editor Toolbar (two overlapping squares) to Merge the Animation Layers together. Animation Layers can be moved horizontally (see below) before being merged together to adjust timing. When merging layers, the layers will be merged into the top selected layers. Animation Layer Controls Location Animation Editor Animation Layer Operation Move Animation Layer Horizontally Double LMB click on the interpolation space of an Animation Layer (solid pink by default) to activate track movement. When the interpolation space of an Animation Layer is highlighted (red by default), the layer can be moved left and right by clicking and dragging with the mouse cursor. To move the Animation Layer to a specific number of frames, when highlighted, RMB clicks on the Animation layer and select 'Move Layer Horizontally', then enter the desired number of frame units to move the Animation Layer. When highlighted, an Animation Layer can also be moved one frame unit at a time by using the Left or Right Arrow Keys. Delete Animation Layer To the left of the Animation Timeline, click on the name of the Animation Layer you would like to delete - highlighting it in grey - and click the "Delete" Key to delete the entire Animation Layer Reorder Animation Layer To the left of the Animation Timeline, click on the name of the Animation Layer you would like to move and drag it above or below the Animation Layer. Animation data for an Animation Layer on top will completely block any animation data on an Animation Layer beneath. Layer Locking &amp Keyframe Visibility Lock an Animation Layer by clicking ON the leftmost yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. Hide an Animation Layer's cached animation by clicking OFF the center yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. Hide an Animation Layer's keyframe markers by clicking OFF the rightmost yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. Animation Layer Selection To select an Animation Layer, click on its title to the left of the animation timeline (it will turn a lighter shade of grey when selected). To add another Animation Layer to the selection, hold down the 'Shift' Key and click on the title of an additional layer. To remove an Animation Layer from the selection, hold down the 'Ctrl' Key and click on the title of any Animation Layer you would like to deselect. Rename Animation layer To rename an animation layer, double-click on its name or right-click on the name of the animation layer and select 'Rename'. Hold down the Shift key to select multiple animation layers, and then follow the above steps to rename them all at once. Animation Editor UI Updates Location Animation Editor Animation Editor Toolbar Operation Animation Editor Icon Additions &amp Updates: Loop Circular Arrow Sets animation timeline playback to loop. Playback Speed 1X Ranges from 1/4X to 8X speed. Merge Selected Animation Layers Two Overlapping Squares Merge selected Animation Layers into a single layer. Cut Selected Animation Layer Scissors Split Animation Layer at current timeline position. Delete Trash Can Deletes Animation Layer or Keyframe depending on selection. Create Keyframe I Creates new Keyframe at current timeline position.

Title: I got H0033 “Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment” error.
Content: The error message occurs when HASP driver is installed improperly in your PC. To check if the HASP driver is installed properly in your PC, type http://localhost:1947 or http://127.0.1:1947 in a browser and see if the following image shows up. If you cant see the image below, it means that the HASP drive is not installed properly. To solve this problem, download HASP driver from the link below and install it. Windows: http://211.191.168.213/data/haspdinst.exe Mac: http://211.191.0.168/213/data/Sentinel_LDK_RTE_Installer.dmg

Title: Video Capture (ver. 2024.0)
Content: Video Capture (ver. 2024.0) Capture a video of recorded animation to view in real time. Steps 1. Open the Animation Editor. 2. Record the animation. 3. Select Video Capture from any of the locations below Main Menu Animation Video Capture Animation Editor Toolbar Video Capture Timeline Menu (Right Click) Video Capture 4. Set the video recording properties. Display Size preset Set the size of the video that will be recorded. The format is shown below. 1920 X 1080 (16:9) 1280 X 720 (16:9) 800 X 450 (16:9) 1024 X 768(4:3) 640 X 480(4:3) Fit to Window : Size of 3D Window Custom Full Screen : Monitor Size Width Set the width of the video to be recorded Height Set the height of the video to be recorded File Format Set the format of the file to save. Window : MP4 / AVI MacOS : MP4 / MOV Save as File Name Name the video. Saving path Specify the location where you want to save the video. Autoseq Numbering The video name is automatically saved with a new number. 5. Click the Capture button. The Capture is executed. When executing capture, the capture button will change to a stop button, and the capture process can be terminated with the stop button. End Result 1. Check the captured video The frame range captured will match the playback start and end in the Animation Editor Settings. If the capture in terminated mid execution, start frame to time terminated will be captured. When the capture ends, the video will be automatically launched to the set media player in your computer. Note: You cannot run video capture without animation. You can only capture the movement of the camera in the 3D Window

Title: Set Fabric Textures (ver. 10)
Content: Objective Express texture or pattern of the fabric. Location Object Browser Fabric Operation Select the menu indicated in Location. Select a fabric. Fabric Property appears in Property Editor. Refer to the below table to set the base texture. PBR (Default) Option Description Texture Repeat Type (ver. 10) Texture Mapping (ver. 11) Repeat Repeatedly display the texture on the pattern. Unified Map Display the texture based on the pattern layout of the UV map. Repeat UV Settings * Repeat U: Size the texture based on U direction. * Repeat V: Size the texture based on V direction. The number 1 means that the texture is repeated once between 0-1 of the UV map. Type Set the appropriate Material Type. Texture Click the explore button and apply a texture image from Library/Folder Note: Click both back and side tabs and deactivate 'Use Same Materials as Front' to apply different materials to other faces of the pattern. Remove Texture Color Remove the default color to apply other colors while retaining the pattern or texture. Normal Map Apply Normal Map image to express uneven texture more realistically. Automatic When a texture is applied, Normal Map is generated by adjusting the Intensity. Higher intensity makes the embossed detail raised off the surface, the lower intensity makes the details lower than the surface. Manual Click the explore or apply the Normal Map image from the Library/Folder Note: Use the normal map image made with the exclusive tool to achieve an accurate normal effect. Also, add a normal map that is different with texture in order to create an extra pattern of surface. Displacement Map (ver.11) Express thickness or bumpiness of fabrics or textures. As displacement maps are grey-scaled, their height is determined by the level of darkness of the grey color. Note: Increase the image resolution and apply the Gaussian Blur effect to express the texture smoothly. Amount Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height. Shift Adjust the distance between the displacement map and the garment surface Clipping Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value. Particle Distance Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes. Note: As more memory is used for lower Particle Distance, it is recommended not to set the Particle Distance below 1 for a wide area. Keep Continuity Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line. Note: Only applicable to Welded OBJs. Color Express each of the fabrics in various colorways Opacity Adjust Opacity to create sheer fabric. Note: When you apply opacity to texture, change Garment Rendering Style as Thick Textured Surface. Alpha Map (ver. 10) Express level of transparency using a grayscale image map RGB Mode The encoded map with alpha value in RGB channel. Alpha Mode The encoded map with alpha value in alpha channel. Roughness Intensity Edit fabric gloss by adjusting Intensity of the Roughness Map Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying Roughness Map. Map Select the Browse button next to the Map option to add a Roughness Map to the selected Fabric style. Map Intensity Adjust the Map's Intensity. Invert Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, the shinny part becomes dull and vice-versa. To use Specular Maps provided in below ver. 6, check this option. Reflection Intensity Greater the Reflection Intensity value is, more reflective than the material or fabric is and vice-versa. Metalness (ver. 10) Adjust metallic level. Higher value makes the surface more metallic. Metalness Map (ver. 10) Partially express metallics using a grayscale image. The white parts of the map appear metallic. Note: When working with Metalness Map, control Roughness Intensity and Reflection Intensity level that are suitable for the metallic texture. (e.g. Roughness Intensity 10, Reflection Intensity 90) For the non-metallic areas(matte), assign the same metalness map to Roughness Map, and turn on Invert. Substance (ver. 10) Set the file format as Substance at the right menu of Material, you can use SBSAR file of Substance which is the main application of physical based rendering. To get a better rendering result for substance materials, enable High-Quality Render on 3D window. Properties Description Substance File Import SBSAR file by clicking 'Explore' or, download SBSAR file by clicking 'Go to Substance Source'. * SBSAR file can be imported by Object Browser&gt Right-click on Fabric item. Preset Choose the preset of SBSAR. Resolution Adjust the image resolution of SBSAR. Custom Properties Edit the properties of SBSAR. Note: Custom Properties are different depending on the property of the file. Refer to the Substance Manual for more detailed information. Note: Clicking on a Fabric from the Fabric List is going to highlight the Patterns where the Fabric is being applied to, in the 3D/2D window. Clicking on a Pattern in the 3D or 2D window is going to highlight the Fabric where it is being applied to, in the Object Browser Fabric Tab.

Title: I am not sure about the subscription pricing model. Is this one of those automatic payment system that bills me every month?
Content: The personal license is a monthly subscription-based license, priced at $39 per month, and it will be automatically billed each month. If you wish, you can opt for a discounted price and subscribe for one year by making a 12-month upfront payment. For enterprise online/offline licenses, only annual purchases are available. However, standalone enterprise license supports an additional monthly subscription at $199 per month. With the annual purchase, there won't be automatic billing, and you will receive an email notification one week before the expiration date. To renew, you will need to proceed with the renewal purchase on the website.

Title: GoZ for Mac
Content: * This feature is not currently supported. It will be fixed soon. GoZ allows direct import/ export of Object between ZBrush and Marvelous Designer. Need to install GoZ installer for GoZ Marvelous Designer Plug-in in ZBrush. GoZ Install for Mac Download GoZ installer and Unzip to GoZApps folder To Activate GoZ function, need to installer GoZ Marvelous Designer Plug-in installer from ZBrush. Download Installer Download installer above, move the installer to GoZApps and unzip. Default Path: /Users/Shared/Pixologic/GoZApps Folder Named MarvelousDesigner will be unzipped. To install GoZ Marvelous Designer, ZBrush need to be installed first. Install GoZ Marvelous Designer from ZBrush After unzip Marvelous Designer folder to GoZApps folder, run ZBrush. ZBrush Main menu &gt Preferences &gt GoZ &gt click Force reinstall. List will be displayed, Click Marvelous Designer from the list. Click 'Install' Button to start install. Once installation is completed, Marvelous Designer will be launched, can find GoZ menu on the Marvelous Designer main menu. Setting Marvelous Designer Path in ZBrush ZBrush Main menu &gt Preferences &gt GoZ &gt Click Update all paths Browse for desired path of Marvelous Designer and select. Run GoZ from Marvelous Designer After installing GoZ Marvelous Designer, can directly export Garment, Avatar and Trims from Marvelous Designer by Run GoZ menu. Location Marvelous Designer Main Menu GoZ Run GoZ Operation Create or load Garment either Avatar to export by GoZ Select the tool according to the Location above. Garment/ Avatar will be added to ZBrush's Subtool according to GoZ export setting. Once the object is exported by GoZ, can edit and update by Run GoZ button. Run GoZ from ZBrush After installing GoZ, can directly export object to Marvelous Designer from ZBrush. Location ZBrush GoZ Operation Create an Object from ZBrush. Select the tool according to the Location above. Garment/ Avatar will be exported to Marvelous Designer according to Marvelous Designer's GoZ import setting. Once the object is exported by GoZ, can edit and update by GoZ button. GoZ Export Settings GoZ Export setting from Marvelous Designer to ZBrush. Location Marvelous Designer Main Menu GoZ Export Settings Operation Object Single Object Exports the selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects Exports the selected object as multiple objects. UnWeld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns. Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Include Avatar Shape: Save the Avatar as part of the file. Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered. *Reset: Reset all GoZ settings to Default. GoZ Import Settings GoZ Import setting from ZBrush to Marvelous Designer. Location Marvelous Designer Main Menu GoZ Import Settings Operation Object Type Load as Avatar Imports the object as an avatar and replaces the original avatar with the imported one. Load as Trim OBJs that are loaded as Trim do not have collision detection with the 3D Garment and will pass through the 3D Garment when simulated. Load as Garment Import an Object as Simulation ready Garment, can adjust Physical property from property editor Scale Manually enter the value. * Reset: Reset all GoZ settings to Default.

Title: Scene and Props Properties (ver.2024.0)
Content: Set the Scene and Props properties. When you select a Scene and Props, its properties appear in the property window. Scene and Props Properties Properties Description Information Model You can change the type of Scene &amp Props Specification Collision (ver. 2024.0) Enable or disable collision handling. When collision is enabled, objects and clothing will collide. Collision Thickness The thickness of the collision treatment on the surface of the object. Can be entered from 0 to 100. Material (Selected) Set the Material of the object. Miscellaneous Mesh Type Indicates the type of object mesh. Element Count Indicates the number of points in the mesh.
